title: Healthy Living
description: Wellness night. Patricia has achieved total beige. Linda is just trying to get her to eat a vegetable.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're listening to the Wellness Hour, here on Snazzie FM. Tonight, we heal. Our first caller has a regimen she swears by. Patricia, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Thank you, Ronnie. So, I follow a very simple, very clean protocol. <p:0.3> I only eat foods that are the color beige.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: ...Beige.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Beige, Barry. Beige is calm. Beige does not inflame.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And how do you feel?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Incredible. <p:0.3> I have not felt a single emotion in eight months.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That... that doesn't sound like health, Patricia.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: It's balance, Barry. <p:0.4> I have achieved total beige.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now I have to say, I admire the commitment.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: I drink only room temperature water, and the broth of a single, very tired potato.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A tired potato.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: It has to be tired, Barry. A nervous potato passes that energy on to you.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And how do you know when a potato is tired, Patricia?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: You look it in the eyes, Ronnie. <p:0.4> A tired potato cannot hold your gaze.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Potatoes don't have eyes. <p:0.3> Well. They have eyes, but they can't see.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: And how would you know what a potato sees, Barry?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: She's turning the questions back on you, Barry. That's a wellness technique.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's not a technique, Ronnie, she just won't answer anything.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: I also do not sleep anymore. <p:0.3> Sleep is a habit, and I have broken it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Think of all the extra hours.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Patricia, when did you last sleep?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: What year is it, Barry?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: ...That's not a good sign, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, honey, no. <p:0.4> Sweetheart, you need to eat a vegetable. A green one. Please.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Green is loud, Linda. I cannot have loud food.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: It's a green bean, dear. It's not a marching band.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: I can hear the green, Linda. <p:0.3> It hums.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, you poor thing. <p:0.4> When did you last have a hot meal, sweetheart?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Heat is a stimulant, Linda. I keep everything at room temperature, including my feelings.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Ronnie, this child needs a casserole and a nap.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Let's keep it respectful, ladies. Both protocols have merit.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: One of these is just not eating, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: I have transcended eating, Barry. <p:0.3> Eating is for people with feelings.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Everybody has feelings, dear. That's just being a person.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Not anymore, Linda. <p:0.4> I am beige now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Linda, I think we have to respect Patricia's journey.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Her journey is going to end in a hospital, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Hospitals are beige, Linda. <p:0.3> I'll feel right at home.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, you sweet, hungry child.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Patricia, before we go, what's on the menu tomorrow?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: A single cracker. <p:0.4> I will look at it for one hour, and then I will put it away.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's not a meal, Ronnie, that's a hostage situation.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: I'm sending you a casserole, Patricia. <p:0.3> It's beige on top. I already checked.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: [surprise-wa] A beige casserole. <p:0.4> Linda, that might be the kindest thing anyone has ever done for me.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And we'll be right back, after this beige word from our sponsor.
